impact:
Confirmed 2026-07-01 by a fresh-session dogfood of the published 1.5.0 MCP server (exactly what a new user gets from `npx codex-claude-bridge@latest`): the very first deliberate review degraded to Gemini-only with degraded.failed=codex, PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE — macOS XProtect had quarantined the @openai/codex-sdk's bundled codex binary (known false-positive; see the codex-binary-xprotect memory and the v1.4.0 handover). Consequences for a real macOS user with no config: deliberate/failover modes silently run single-provider (Gemini), and single-codex mode fails outright. The 1.4.0 escape hatch (config codex_path / CODEX_PATH env) works but is manual and only discoverable by reading the error text — while a perfectly good system codex often already exists (this machine: ~/.local/bin/codex, v0.142.5).

PROPOSED FIX (auto-discovery fallback, config always wins): in createCodexBackend (src/backends/codex.ts:242, the `config.codex_path ?? process.env.CODEX_PATH` chain), when NO explicit override is set, preflight the bundled binary (cheap spawn, e.g. `codex --version`, or reuse the existing PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE classification on first failure); on failure, probe in order: `which codex` on PATH, then well-known locations (~/.local/bin/codex, /opt/homebrew/bin/codex, /usr/local/bin/codex). Use the first that runs, and narrate the substitution on stderr ([codex-bridge] bundled codex unusable, using /path/to/codex) so the behavior is transparent. An explicit codex_path/CODEX_PATH must still win unconditionally and never be second-guessed. Consider caching the probe result per-process to avoid re-probing per review. Alternative/simpler variant: keep the failure but extend the PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE tip to name any discovered system codex path ready to paste into codex_path.

Validation for the fix: the degraded marker from T-028 made this diagnosable in one read (degraded.failed + reason) — keep that behavior for the no-binary-found case.
resolution: Fixed: the codex backend now auto-discovers a working system codex when the SDK's bundled binary cannot run and no explicit override is set. New src/backends/codex-binary.ts: discoverCodexBinary() checks the caller's PATH directories in order, then well-known install locations (~/.local/bin, /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin); a candidate must both be executable AND pass a `--version` run probe (5s timeout) — an XProtect-hit file can be present yet killed on spawn, so existence alone is not trusted. In createCodexBackend, the turn runner retries once when a review fails PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: recovery is memoized as a shared promise (concurrent failing reviews await ONE discovery and all benefit — review-round finding), never rejects (a discovery throw resolves to not-found, preserving the Result contract — review-round finding), rebuilds the SDK client via codexPathOverride, and narrates the substitution on stderr with a codex_path pin hint. An explicit codex_path/CODEX_PATH fully disables discovery (never second-guess a pin). When nothing is found, the PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE error gains an "auto-discovery: no working system codex found" note. README: codex_path documented (was entirely missing), Troubleshooting row added, stale max_file_size removed from the example (T-031 leftover). Tests: 11 discovery unit tests (all seams injected) + 10 recovery wiring tests incl. concurrency and throw-containment locks; 807 total green. LIVE-VERIFIED end-to-end on the real failure: config without codex_path in single mode → bundled binary unusable → discovered /Users/amirshayegh/.local/bin/codex → narrated → retried → codex served the review. Two-round deliberate bridge review: both accepted majors fixed (shared-promise memoization, throw containment) + shadowing nitpick fixed; the repeated 'codex is const' critical contested as a diff-visibility false positive (declaration is `let codex` at codex.ts:266, typecheck green — ISS-020 pattern, both providers wrong the same way in round 1).
title: Out-of-box Codex is broken on macOS: XProtect quarantines the SDK's bundled binary; add auto-discovery fallback to a system codex
